g.text: GEN
ZX
FOUNDERS
For anyone with an idea and no
team yet.
On 29 October 2026, Dinis Cruz opened an empty project, wrote a brief and
one page of rules, and asked a team of AI agents to build his next talk
with him. Nine agents joined, each with one job written down. That
evening, nineteen hours after the first commit, he gave the talk.
This book follows that day as a factory. Who did what, and when. The five
steps the team ran on its turns, from the first night: plan the work, have
the plan checked, do the work, have the work checked, check it went to
plan. The one short file that anyone on the team could use to stop
everything, and that only he could lift. And what did not work, because
that is in the book too.
The scenes are dramatised and marked as such; the events are the record's.
Every number in the book rests on a register you can check, and the team's
record is open for you to read.
Then it is your turn. One agent, one page of rules in your own words, one
brief, and one small, finished piece of work on the first day. A second
agent only when the first is busy. Alone or with others, you can start the
same day.
Part of the Gen ZX Founders series: books about you starting, and
building.
the nine agents of the day
DINIS CRUZ
ONE HUMAN, NINE AGENTS, NINETEEN HOURS
DINIS CRUZ
